phase, m = 0.3, 5
u, prep = phase_gate_example(phase)
instrument = build_iterative_qpe(m, u, prep)

feedback = dynamic_distribution(instrument)
reference = qpe_distribution(phase, m)
conventional = simulate_qpe(build_qpe(m, u, prep), m)
np.testing.assert_allclose(feedback, reference, atol=3e-13, rtol=0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(feedback, conventional, atol=3e-13, rtol=0)
print({"output_bits": m, "quantum_wires": instrument.num_qubits,
       "feedback_reference_max_error": float(np.max(abs(feedback-reference))),
       "feedback_static_max_error": float(np.max(abs(feedback-conventional))),
       "method": "actual ideal instrument branch enumeration"})

Guarded floating matrix checks and small instrument enumeration are numerical
evidence, not a formal synthesis interval or hardware confidence certificate.
Encoder, readout, controller and code-exposure fits are declared scenarios.
Tracked Pauli bases, lattice geometry, decoder throughput and factory/data
handoff remain conditional assumptions. Offline compilation and
presentation-only final reporting time are excluded. Physical qubit counts
cover quantum patches and factories. This separate comparison preserves all
earlier static QPE projections and the frozen Grover baseline.

The tested feedback distributions cover grid and off-grid phases, all tested output-bit sizes through five, global phases, a Y eigenstate and non-eigenstate mixtures. Primitive lowering preserves tested instrument probabilities. Independent review additionally checked entangled targets and conjugated multi-qubit eigenstates. The instrument checker is capped at eight quantum/classical bits, 4,096 top-level operations and 1,024 branches. It drops numerically zero branches below
and checks remaining total probability. These are bounded ideal numerical checks, not a physical simulator or a Lean theorem.
The scalar-median confidence contract and its phase branch-cut assumption are
. No noisy-hardware inference or circular median is claimed.

from openquantum.qft_qpe import phase_gate_example, build_iterative_qpe, dynamic_distribution
unitary, preparation = phase_gate_example(0.3)
circuit = build_iterative_qpe(5, unitary, preparation)
probabilities = dynamic_distribution(circuit)
. The measured/reset QASM is an instrument, not a coherent unitary oracle. Coherent use of a unitary subroutine requires its unmeasured source circuit with global phase preserved.
